subject: Request: compact boundary synthesis & diagram for SIG/CAIQ - Dedicated + Private
messages:
From: Elena Torres <security@nimbusfinance.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 25 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: compact boundary synthesis & diagram for SIG/CAIQ - Dedicated + Private

Hi Vivek / Kimberly / Jonas,

Thanks for the quick intro on the call earlier. Nimbus is preparing its SIG + CAIQ packet for a vendor security review and we need a short, customer-facing deliverable that accomplishes two things:

- A compact (1–2 page) boundary narrative that describes how Redwood isolates customer workloads across Dedicated and Private deployment modes (control plane, data plane, egress controls, KMS/keys).
- A single-page network topology/diagram (PNG) showing the high-level isolation model — labelled boxes for customer tenant, dedicated GPU pool, private VPC, control plane, and egress breakouts — plus a short table mapping the diagram elements to the SIG/CAIQ questions (network segregation, control plane partitioning, egress logging/retention, KMS ownership).

Constraints: Nimbus needs something concise we can attach to the SIG packet and also redact if necessary. Target delivery for an initial draft is EOD next Wednesday (5 May).

Two quick clarifications for scope: we need both Dedicated and Private described (we will evaluate both), and we prefer a short explicit statement about whether customers have access to egress logs and for how long those logs are retained.

If you can send an initial draft + diagram link, we’ll review and give a shortlist of follow-ups. If there’s a better person to own the technical bit (network diagram + KMS callouts), feel free to loop them in.

Thanks — happy to sync if it’s easier.

Elena Torres
Security Engineer, Nimbus Finance
security@nimbusfinance.com

Attachments referenced: None in this message

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <security@nimbusfinance.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 25 Apr 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: compact boundary synthesis & diagram for SIG/CAIQ - Dedicated + Private

Hi Elena — thanks for the clarity and the timeline.

We can put together a concise boundary narrative + single-page diagram that maps directly to the SIG/CAIQ items you called out. To set expectations:
- We’ll produce a 1–2 page narrative that covers Dedicated and Private in parallel, focusing on isolation primitives (tenant network, service/compute rings, control plane separation, KMS ownership model and HSM options) and the observable controls (egress logging, flow logs, retention, and access).
- A one-page PNG diagram with labeled zones and a small mapping table to SIG question IDs.

Questions to confirm:
1) Acceptable retention window for log examples in the narrative? If Nimbus has a minimum requirement (e.g., 90 days) we’ll include an explicit statement.
2) Are you asking for certified (SOC 2) language or a neutral technical narrative for SIG/CAIQ? We can tailor wording for auditor consumption or for a gating security review.

Kimberly and Jonas, can you own a first-pass draft? I’m happy to review and provide the business/sales framing. Target internal delivery to Elena by 2026-05-01 (EOD) for a reviewed draft, final by 2026-05-05 if that aligns with the customer ask.

Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Security & Compliance - Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <security@nimbusfinance.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 25 Apr 2026 13:48:00 -0700
Subject: Draft: segmentation narrative + diagram (attached)

Elena — thanks, looping back with a compact draft and a diagram. I’ve attached a short narrative (PDF) and a single-page PNG diagram. High-level callouts included in the document:

- Deployment modes: Dedicated (pooled GPUs allocated to a single enterprise tenant with network-level segmentation) vs Private (customer-managed VPC with Redwood Private control plane integration).
- Control plane: Hosted control plane (for Hosted/Dedicated) runs in a separate, restricted control domain with no direct access to tenant data. For Private we state an optional customer-managed control plane; when enabled, audit and KMS operations can be brokered via an encrypted control channel.
- Network isolation primitives: per-tenant VPC/subnet, security groups, per-tenant route tables where applicable, and a sidecar enforcement layer (control-plane proxy + local policy enforcer) in Private mode.
- KMS & keys: Default model is Redwood-managed KMS keys for Hosted/Dedicated (keys in Redwood KMS), with an option for customer-provided keys (Bring Your Own Key) for Private deployments. We included wording for HSM-backed keys where customers require FIPS-level attestation.
- Egress & logging: Egress flows are NATed at tenant boundary; we capture flow logs and application-layer egress events. Typical retention is 90 days by default; we explain how retention can be extended for Private with customer-managed log storage. We also call out how customers can access logs (read-only exports and a secure S3 export link).

I’ve kept the narrative deliberately non-prescriptive and auditor-friendly. The attachments in this message: segmentation-narrative-draft-v1.pdf and compact-boundary-diagram-v1.png.

Action items for Nimbus: please confirm whether 90 days retention meets your baseline. Also confirm if you want explicit SOC 2 control language — currently the narrative is neutral and maps to SIG/CAIQ items; we can create an additional SOC 2 appendix if needed.

Kimberly Park
Principal Security Architect, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

From: Elena Torres <security@nimbusfinance.com>

Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 25 Apr 2026 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft: segmentation narrative + diagram (attached)

Kimberly — thank you, this is exactly the style we needed and very clear. A couple of quick follow-ups from our security review checklist:

1) Egress logs: can you add one sentence that explicitly states whether customers can retrieve their egress logs on-demand (and the mechanism)? The line about "read-only exports and secure S3 export link" is good, but the reviewer wants explicit confirmation that exports are customer-triggerable and that log integrity is verifiable.
2) Retention: 90 days is fine as a baseline, but please clarify if Redwood offers longer retention as a paid option (or for Private deployments) and whether the retention extension maintains the same tamper-evidence guarantees.

If you can reply inline in the doc or send a one-paragraph update, we’ll slot it into the SIG packet and push this through our gate.

Best,
Elena Torres
Security Engineer, Nimbus Finance
security@nimbusfinance.com
